## Astronomical 0.2.110
### Faster decoding for the dense Qwen 27B
A dense Qwen 27B (4-bit) now decodes with DFlash2 draft trees when its DFlash2 drafter is installed in the same model library. A small drafter model proposes several tokens at a time, and the 27B checks a whole tree of proposals in one pass, so every token in the reply is still the 27B's own choice.
Measured on an M5 Pro with the 27B and its drafter:
| Request | Before | Now | |---|---|---| | Coding request, temperature 0.7 | about 13 tok/s | 67 to 71 tok/s | | Chat request, temperature 1.0 | about 13 tok/s | 47 to 48 tok/s | | Reply after a 10,000-token prompt, temperature 1.0 | about 13 tok/s | about 35 tok/s |
Prompt processing speed is unchanged, and a follow-up turn in a conversation still reuses the work of the earlier turns.
What to know:
- It needs a Mac whose GPU has the M5 matrix units. On other Macs, and for models without a matching drafter, decoding is unchanged. - Requests with images, JSON-constrained output or a repetition penalty use ordinary decoding, as before. - Greedy replies are the same text ordinary decoding gives. Sampled replies are drawn from the same distribution, with a sampler keyed to the request's seed, so a seeded request repeats exactly. - The drafter is loaded beside the 27B at 4 bits, so the pair uses somewhat more memory than the 27B alone.
### Compatibility
- Settings, conversations, downloaded models and the `astro_ssd_prompt_cache` are preserved. - No configuration changes are required.
### Distribution
The disk image is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. Existing installs receive this version through the built-in update check.
### Acknowledgements
Draft-tree decoding follows the approach of the TensorFold engine and uses the DFlash2 drafter published by Z Lab; both are credited in the third-party notices.
